_readme: Machine-readable cadence expectations for the standing 'are the bots alive?' check.
docs/agents/runners.md is the human registry and stays the source of truth for
WHAT each runner does. This file is only the observable-artifact contract used by
scripts/marjorie/standing-checks.mjs: for each runner, what does GitHub see, and
how often should it see it. Keeping it separate from runners.md means the check
can be updated without touching a doc another agent owns.
'perDay' is the artifact rate the registry claims. 'maxAgeHours' is how long
silence is tolerated before the runner is called dark — deliberately ~1.25x the
nominal period, so one skipped run is not an alert but two are.
'checkable: false' entries are the honest gap: these runners produce PRs against
supabase/seed/** with no branch prefix and no distinguishing label, so no query
can separate them from any other content PR. They are listed anyway, because a
monitoring blind spot that is written down is a ticket and one that isn't is a
surprise. Fix = give each a branch prefix; noted in the PR body.
'disabled: true' entries mirror a ⛔ row in runners.md: the trigger is off ON
PURPOSE (warm spare / superseded). They are kept so the check can say 'disabled
by design' instead of 'dark' — on 2026-09-05 four of the seven 'dark runners'
the brief flagged were triggers the founders had switched off five days earlier.
Re-enable here the same day the trigger is re-enabled in runners.md.
'brief-comment' matches a comment on a Founders' Brief issue whose first line
is exactly the given HTML anchor — how Kevin's daily desk reports since T-10.
